title: The five sheaths: food (2.1)
hook: a set of nesting dolls, and the outermost one is made of last week's dinners

segments.voice: Yesterday: mother, father, teacher, guest, each to be honored as god. Your line was matri devo bhava.

Open a set of nesting dolls. Inside the big painted one, a smaller one; inside that, a smaller one, finer and finer, until you reach the tiny one in the middle. The Taittiriya Upanishad's second book takes a person apart the same way, five layers deep, and the next three days open them one by one. Today, the outermost doll. It's made of something you ate this week.
screen: `A DOLL INSIDE A DOLL.` → `FIVE LAYERS DEEP.` → `THE OUTERMOST IS MADE OF FOOD.`

segments.voice: The book opens with a promise: the one who knows Brahman reaches the highest. And a definition in four Sanskrit words: satyam jnanam anantam brahma. Brahman is truth, knowledge, the infinite. Then a creation story, told like a relay. From this self, space came. From space, wind. From wind, fire. From fire, water. From water, earth. From earth, plants. From plants, food. From food, the person. So the person, the text says, is made of the essence of food. Annamaya: made of food. And it draws that person as a bird. This is the head. This is the right wing. This is the left wing. This is the body. This, underneath, is the tail, the foundation. Then a short hymn to food. From food all creatures are born. By food they live. Into food, in the end, they go. Food is the eldest of beings, so it's called the medicine of everything. Read plainly, it's something you can check. The hands holding your phone were, not long ago, rice, lentils, bread, an apple. And then the text says: different from this one made of food, inside it, is another self, made of breath. That's tomorrow. Later Hindu teachers call these layers the five koshas, the five sheaths, like a sword's scabbard. The Taittiriya itself doesn't use that word. It just keeps saying: inside this one, another self.
screen: `SATYAM JNANAM ANANTAM BRAHMA.` · `SPACE, WIND, FIRE, WATER, EARTH, FOOD.` · `THE PERSON MADE OF FOOD, SHAPED LIKE A BIRD.` · `INSIDE IT, ANOTHER SELF.` · then, large: `ANNAMAYA.`

segments.voice: Feel the body's weight on the seat, its warmth, its pulse, the heaviness of the hands, and remember, gently, that this was food: grain, fruit, water, sunlight, a farmer's work, someone's cooking. Let a little thanks go to all of it, then feel the body again just as it is, the first layer, the one you can touch.
Annamaya, made of food. In the Taittiriya, the outermost self: the body, built from what a person eats, and the first of the five layers.
Your line: the medicine of everything. Food is the eldest of beings. That's day three hundred ninety-one.

howItsDone: Many Hindus offer food to God before eating and receive it back as prasad; in Vedanta and in yoga teaching, the five koshas drawn from this Upanishad are used to describe the layers of a person, starting with the body made of food.

notes: The index word is 'The five sheaths' (the title's head); kept exactly.
Creation sequence (2.1): ātman → ākāśa → vāyu → agni → āpaḥ → pṛthivī → oṣadhayaḥ → anna → puruṣa. Confirm.
Bird form of each self (head, right wing, left wing, body/ātman, tail/foundation): 2.1. Confirm.
'Food is the eldest of beings, so it is called the medicine of all' (2.2): paraphrased.
Pañcakośa as a later term (e.g., Vivekachudamani, Panchadashi), not in the Taittiriya itself: confirm.
'Over the next three days' assumes days 391–393 cover the five layers (food; breath and mind; understanding and bliss).
